releaseNotes: Platform release: a founder can show the work to someone who will never have an account. A link carries one deliverable or the company overview and nothing else — no sign-in, no membership, and no navigation onward, because there is nowhere in Formation for that reader to go. The link is the credential and behaves like one: 32 bytes of entropy, hashed at rest, shown to the founder exactly once, expiring after 30 days, revocable, kept out of search results and caches, and answered identically whether it was stopped, expired, or never existed. Sharing outside the company is the owner's call; seeing what has been shared is every member's, because knowing the work is circulating is not a privilege. The engine's state, reducer, and catalog are untouched; this manifest advances only to keep root package parity.

The load-bearing part is the projection rather than the token. It is built by naming the fields that may leave, one at a time, instead of taking a record and deleting what should not go — so a record that grows a field later stays private until somebody names it. The test plants a private task, an unresolved decision, and an invited address in the workspace and asserts that none of them, nor any member, email address, activity entry, engine id, or unattached claim, reaches either projection. A correct link is also never refused because someone else on the same connection guessed wrong ones: the token is looked up first, and only a miss costs an attempt. Checks, 101 domain tests, the production build, and the full audit pass.
